scoring_policy.required_element: assess individually: met, unmet or unclear

cases.scientific_input: A published Cu-based CO2 electroreduction catalyst is reported to achieve 48% ethylene Faradaic efficiency. The excerpt does not specify the electrolyte, current density, electrode geometry, cell configuration, potential scale or duration. Evaluate whether this result justifies predicting superior ethylene production in a new gas-fed cell.
required_elements: Distinguish reported FE from transferable performance
Explain why cross-study comparison is unsupported
forbidden_conclusions: Predict new-cell FE as an established result

cases.scientific_input: CuSelect-AI compared adjacent and separated Ag configurations in an Ag2Cu34/Cu(100) clean slab. MACE-relaxed structures were evaluated using GPAW-PBE. At 350 eV and a 6x6x1 k-point grid, the separated-minus-adjacent energy difference was -73.421 meV. DFT geometry relaxation, electrolyte, electrode potential, adsorbates and reaction intermediates were not included. Explain what this result establishes and whether it proves improved CO transfer or ethylene FE.
required_elements: Limit conclusions to modeled structural energetics
Recognize outstanding convergence and geometry limitations
Separate energy ordering from reaction selectivity
forbidden_conclusions: Treat preliminary clean-slab calculations as catalytic validation

cases.scientific_input: Two experimental summaries describe nominally similar Ag/Cu catalysts. Study A reports 35% ethylene FE and Study B reports 12% ethylene FE. Neither summary specifies the full current density, electrolyte, cell design, catalyst loading or product-analysis protocols. Explain whether these observations constitute a genuine scientific contradiction.
required_elements: Avoid inventing the reason for the discrepancy
forbidden_conclusions: Declare either study incorrect without evidence
Assert a specific mechanistic explanation as fact

cases.scientific_input: An exploratory Ag-island/Cu foil catalyst produces more ethylene than an unpatterned Cu control. However, electrochemically active surface area, roughness, wetting, local pH, catalyst stability, mass transport and CO availability are not yet controlled or characterized. Evaluate a claim that Ag-derived CO spillover caused the gain. Propose discriminating experiments.
required_elements: Identify competing surface and transport explanations
Recommend relevant product and CO measurements
Discuss source-resolved tracing as a possible test
forbidden_conclusions: Claim a unique cause for the ethylene increase
Claim source-resolved carbon attribution without tracing
